summary: Set up ephemeral audit workspace (Confluence template + Slack threads) with action-item -> Jira automation
description:
Issue summary:
Request to create a templated, ephemeral audit workspace for upcoming external audit of model governance documents. Workspace should include: a Confluence space with a live-edit Audit Review template (checklist, decisions log, redaction placeholder), an ephemeral Slack channel provisioned and linked to the space, and automation that converts Confluence checklist action items into Jira subtasks under a designated parent issue.

Background and impact:
- The Model Governance team will host external auditors for 2 weeks starting 2026-04-06. They need a space where documents can be collaboratively reviewed and action items tracked as Jira tasks.
- Current process is manual (copy/paste) and produces fragmented action-tracking. This automation reduces audit overhead and ensures traceability.

Requirements (high level):
1) Create a Confluence space called "Audit-Review-2026-Q2" using a reusable template "Audit Review Checklist (live)". Template must include: reviewer roster macro, decision log table, action-item checkboxes with an "Export to Jira" tag.
2) Provision ephemeral Slack channel #audit-2026-q2 with 30-day auto-archive policy; channel should be created in the Model Governance workspace and automatically add group @model-governance and external-auditors-service-account when approved.
3) Create automation (Confluence -> Jira) that: when an action item checkbox is added or marked with tag [JIRA_CREATE], it creates a Jira sub-task under parent INT-627841-ACTIONS (ephemeral parent) with fields: summary, assignee placeholder, due-date derived from Confluence label. Automation should post a link back in the Confluence comment.
4) Provision a scoped service account (audit-bot@redwood-internal) with least privilege to create tickets and post comments; add audit logging to show who triggered an automation.
5) Retention: space content should be retained for 90 days after the audit end date (audit end = 2026-04-20), then archived to a restricted read-only archive with export available to InfoSec. Slack channel messages should have a retention exception for 45 days, then be exported to the archive space and the channel removed.
6) Security: PII redaction placeholders must be present in the template and automation must flag any page containing strings matching regex for SSN/email patterns and automatically anonymize or tag for manual redaction.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence space created and visible to @model-governance and selected auditors.
- Slack channel exists and shows a message from audit-bot confirming linkage.
- Creating an action item with [JIRA_CREATE] in Confluence results in a Jira sub-task visible under the parent issue and includes a back-link to the Confluence page.
- Audit-bot writes to an audit log (Confluence comment and Jira comment) with a timestamp and actor.
- InfoSec has reviewed and signed off on the PII redaction behavior.

Runbook / steps to perform:
- Step 1: Create Confluence space using template and set permissions.
- Step 2: Create service account and add to secrets vault; generate API key with expiry.
- Step 3: Provision Slack channel and attach a webhook/Slash command for audit-bot.
- Step 4: Deploy Jira automation rule (or use internal automation service) that listens to Confluence webhooks, creates sub-tasks, and logs events.
- Step 5: Test end-to-end with a small page and one action item; verify log entries.
- Step 6: Present to InfoSec and get approval; update acceptance criteria.

Notes:
- Prefer existing automation infra (internal-automation-service) rather than external third-party add-ons to keep audit trail centralized.
- Parent issue INT-627841-ACTIONS will be created in the Model Governance project; this ticket will own the automation config and be linked from generated sub-tasks.
comments: Priya Raman (2026-03-09): Opening this request on behalf of Model Governance. External auditors will need a consolidated space and we need the automation to ensure no action items fall through the cracks.

Ethan Cole (2026-03-09): Assigned. Quick clarifying questions: 1) Who are the external auditor accounts (emails) to add? 2) Do we require MFA for the service account? 3) Which Jira project should parent INT-627841-ACTIONS live in?

Priya Raman (2026-03-10): Auditor emails: auditor.alpha@external-audit.com, auditor.beta@external-audit.com. Service account should be short-lived key (30-day) and rotated; MFA not required for service accounts but key must be stored in vault. Parent Jira project: MGOV (Model Governance).

Security (InfoSec) - L. Nguyen (2026-03-10): We need to review the PII redaction regex and confirm that automated anonymization is reversible only by InfoSec. Please include a test page with synthetic PII for validation.

Ethan Cole (2026-03-11): Plan: I'll provision the space and channel in staging and run E2E tests by 2026-03-15. I'll create the service account with a 30-day key and put the key in the secrets vault. Posting preliminary automation rule in linked PR once drafted.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-09 - Checked existing templates: Found 'Audit Review Checklist' draft in Confluence templates but it lacks action-item -> Jira integration.
Potential path: use internal automation-service to bridge Confluence webhook -> createIssue API in Jira.

2026-03-10 - Slack provisioning: Verified Model Governance workspace allows app-level webhooks; ephemeral channel auto-archive can be set via channel property but needs a scheduled job to export messages before deletion.

2026-03-11 - Service account considerations: Must be created in SSO as a managed service principal and given only 'browse' permissions in Confluence plus 'create issues' in the MGOV Jira project scoped to the parent. Keys will be timebound.

Slack channel #audit-2026-q2 exists and shows initial audit-bot message linking to Confluence space
Action item with [JIRA_CREATE] tag creates a Jira sub-task with back-link
Automation logs (Confluence comment + Jira comment) include timestamp and service account identity
PII redaction detection triggers a flag and InfoSec confirms behavior on test page
resolution: In progress: provisioning in staging underway. Next steps: create service account, implement automation rule, run E2E tests, and submit InfoSec test page. Planned completion for initial E2E in staging by 2026-03-15.
